claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can be used to identify ferromagnetic ground states.
A spin-polarized solution that is lower in energy than a nonmagnetic solution is energetically favored over the nonmagnetic state.
Comparing spin-polarized and non-spin-polarized DFT total energies can determine whether magnetic ordering is favorable.
Ground-state DFT calculations are conducted at 0 K or under conditions where the ground state is accessible.
Appropriate treatment of electron exchange and correlation is required for the calculation.
The calculated band structure and magnetic-moment distribution mediate stabilization of the ferromagnetic state.
Significant magnetic moments together with lower energy of a spin-polarized state indicate exchange-correlation stabilization of magnetic ordering.
A lower-energy spin-polarized configuration relative to a non-spin-polarized configuration indicates a ferromagnetic ground state.
Non-spin-polarized DFT provides a reference total energy without magnetic ordering.
Conventional DFT is robust for systems that it describes well.
Conventional DFT may be less accurate for strongly correlated materials that require beyond-DFT treatments.
Computed energy differences and magnetic moments can depend on the exchange-correlation functional and computational parameters.
Experimental measurements such as SQUID magnetometry may be needed to validate the prediction.
An equal or lower non-spin-polarized energy would falsify the proposed ferromagnetic-ground-state assignment under the stated comparison.
Negligible computed magnetic moments would falsify the proposed ferromagnetic-ground-state assignment.
